title: Tiger Woods reacts after Team USA’s Presidents Cup win as Trump praises comeback
description: Tiger Woods reacted after Team USA’s record Presidents Cup comeback, while Donald Trump praised the 17-13 victory at Medinah.
fullText:
Tiger Woods has spoken after Team USA turned a three-point deficit into a historic victory at Medinah Country Club. The Americans entered Sunday trailing the International Team 10.5-7.5 after three days of competition. They answered by taking 9.5 of 12 singles points on Sunday. Jacob Bridgeman clinched the trophy before the remaining matches were completed.

The 17-13 result gave the United States its 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title. It also produced the largest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history. Woods, who captained the U.S. to victory in 2019, reacted to the finish with a brief message. His reaction came after the Americans completed a comeback that had appeared unlikely entering the final day.

Woods posted his reaction on social media after the Americans completed their comeback. "What a comeback!" Woods wrote, congratulating Team USA on an "incredible Presidents Cup victory" and calling it a "Great team win."

His message also highlighted how difficult the situation had become before Sunday's singles. Woods noted that the Americans needed the matchups to go their way, and the results ultimately did so.

The reaction carried extra context because Woods remains closely tied to the Presidents Cup. He played in nine editions, served as captain in 2019, and helped the Americans recover from an early deficit at Royal Melbourne that year. His public response also came immediately after a victory that echoed the resilience of that earlier U.S. comeback.

Team USA needed eight points from 12 singles matches to reach the 15.5 points required to win. Cameron Young started the charge by beating Ryo Hisatsune 3 and 2, while Justin Thomas followed with a 5-and-3 victory over Corey Conners.

Scottie Scheffler, Chris Gotterup and Collin Morikawa then added crucial points as the Americans kept pressure on the International side. Patrick Cantlay created one of the day's biggest moments when he holed a 57-foot putt from off the 16th green against Adam Scott.

Morikawa's 1-up win over Hideki Matsuyama put the Americans ahead 13.5-12.5. Jackson Koivun then defeated Si Woo Kim 2 up, leaving Bridgeman in position to clinch the Cup with his match against Min Woo Lee. Xander Schauffele later added another full point, while Russell Henley halved his match to close the final score at 17-13.

President Donald Trump attended the final day as the Presidents Cup's honorary chairman. He addressed the players from the first tee before the singles session and later took part in the trophy presentation.

After the victory, Trump praised the American team while speaking to reporters at Joint Base Andrews. He called the team "unbelievable," described the result as a "big, big win" and said those watching had witnessed a "very historic event" in sports, golf and for the country.

Snedeker also credited Trump with helping inspire the team. The captain said Trump told him he had "brought some juice" for the Americans and added that he would give Trump credit if the day turned in their favor. The comments placed Trump's presence directly into the post-match conversation surrounding the comeback.

Woods' connection to the event goes well beyond his captaincy in 2019. He represented the United States in the Presidents Cup in 1998, 2000, 2003, 2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2013 and 2019.

His most memorable Presidents Cup role came in 2019, when he served as a playing captain at Royal Melbourne. Woods went 3-0 as a player and selected himself as one of his captain's picks, while the Americans overcame a 10-8 deficit entering Sunday to win 16-14.

The 2026 comeback added another chapter to Woods' long association with the event. Team USA's 17-13 victory improved the Americans' all-time Presidents Cup record to 14-1-1, while the International Team remained without a victory since its lone title in 1998.

Woods' nine Presidents Cup appearances, stretching from 1998 through 2019, along with his role as U.S. captain in 2019, show how long he has remained connected to the competition across multiple generations of players.

Fun fact: Medinah No. 3 has a particularly strong connection to Tiger Woods. He won both PGA Championships played there, taking the 1999 title by one stroke over Sergio Garcia and the 2006 championship by five strokes over Shaun Micheel.

The final-day rally surpassed the previous Presidents Cup record for a comeback entering singles. Woods' 2019 U.S. team had previously held that mark after entering Sunday trailing 10-8 at Royal Melbourne.

This year's Americans faced an even larger challenge, entering Sunday three points behind. The 9.5-2.5 singles advantage produced a four-point final margin and completed the largest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history.

Bridgeman's clinching point came in his Presidents Cup debut, while Koivun finished his first appearance undefeated. Their performances added a younger layer to a team that also relied on established stars such as Scheffler, Thomas, Morikawa, Cantlay, and Schauffele.

The International Team had led 7-3 after Friday's foursomes and still held a three-point advantage entering Sunday, but the Americans produced wins across the lineup instead of relying on a single player to carry the comeback.

The turnaround featured balance, with nine U.S. players recording singles wins. The Americans finished Sunday singles 9-2-1, completing the 17-13 victory.

Tiger Woods congratulated Team USA after its 17-13 Presidents Cup victory at Medinah.

The Americans erased a 10.5-7.5 deficit by winning 9.5 of 12 Sunday singles points.

Jacob Bridgeman clinched the Cup in his Presidents Cup debut against Min Woo Lee.

Donald Trump praised the U.S. victory, while Brandt Snedeker credited his presence with inspiring the team.

The victory gave Team USA its 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title and a 14-1-1 overall record.

title: Top HS football games of the week: No. 10 Los Gatos visits No. 2 Pittsburg
description: When No. 10 Los Gatos travels to No. 2 Pittsburg on Friday, it will be a matchup of public school powers succeeding despite losing players to private school recruiting.
fullText:
It doesn't get much better on the high school football scene Friday when 10th-ranked Los Gatos (3-1), a 16-time Central Coast Section champion, travels 70 miles to face five-time defending North Coast Section Division 1 champion Pittsburg (2-2), the Chronicle's No. 2 team.

What makes this matchup so attractive to some, and so impressive, is that this is a pair of public school programs - the visiting Wildcats surrounded in the South Bay by private school powers St. Francis, Mitty, Valley Christian, King's Academy-Sunnyvale, and Atherton's Menlo School and Sacred Heart Prep.

Pittsburg, meanwhile, really has to compete from the private sector only by the kings of Northern California football, De La Salle-Concord.

Both Los Gatos and Pittsburg have lost countless top prospects to the private school powers, yet both have been a model of consistency for decades.

"We're very lucky at Los Gatos," said 14th-year head coach Mark Krail, who took over for Butch Cattolico (264-62-7, according to CalHiSports) in 2013. "We are a small town in the midst of Silicon Valley. As coaches we play to that notion. Our kids grow up in town and attend Los Gatos football games at a very young age. … The kids coming in all know each other and have grown up together. To me that is true brotherhood as opposed to some private schools that draw from multiple counties."

Krail, who previously coached at Pioneer-San Jose and Santa Clara, has gone 116-42 at Los Gatos. He's won 223 games overall.

Cattolico, a Pittsburg Hall of Fame player, won 14 of Los Gatos' championships and Krail the last two in 2019 and 2023. The Wildcats won their only NorCal regional title in 2023, losing in the state 2-A state championship 45-42. Last season they beat private school powers St. Francis (14-7) and Palma-Salinas (45-21) before losing in the Division 1 title game to Serra.

In 2024, they eliminated WCAL powers Serra (14-7) and Riordan (35-28), only to lose to St. Francis (27-7) in the CCS Open Division title game.

"One real key for us is that we are able to keep most kids in town," Krail said. "That is enough to compete with anyone. So many public schools are having their neighborhood kids taken by the private schools. Let's face it, the privates are in an arms race to accumulate as much talent as they can. They say they don't recruit, but they do. They say they don't give scholarships, but they do. They say they don't lower academic standards, they do. They are all so wrapped in each other that they have total disregard for public school programs or rosters.

"One of our stronger local public school programs lost four kids this offseason to three different WCAL schools. Something is wrong with that."

Rather than rail against private schools, Krails said he'd rather focus on what the Wildcats do well, all possible due to the "massive support" from administration, from the superintendent on down. … Our athletic director Ken Perrotti is the best in California. We are very lucky."

Coaching continuity and player development is also key, Krail said. "We are fortunate to have a freshman team, which plays private schools. We typically are beaten at that level, but by the time our players move through the JV team and onto varsity they have sacrificed so much and worked so hard they have developed into quality players and teams that are able to compete with the best private schools. … I would stack up our (coaching staffs) with any staff in CCS. I am very lucky to work with such great mentors and coaches."

Quarterback development is a prime example at Los Gatos, where Jack Siri (42 of 74, 623 yards, six touchdowns) sat last year behind All-Metro senior Callum Schweitzer (2,462 yards, 25 TDs), who in 2024 shared time with senior starter Scotty Brennan (son of former San Jose State, now Arizona coach Brent Brennan).

"We coach whoever attends our school, and don't need to recruit outside kids to be successful," Krail said.

Playing Pittsburg every season has sharpened the competitive edges for the Wildcats, who have lost to the Pirates the last three years in terrific games, 30-27, 37-20 and 37-27. This might be Pittsburg's most talented team, proven in tight losses to nationally ranked St. John Bosco (26-14) and at Mission Viejo (42-35).

Both teams had byes last week to rest up for what promises to be another good one. Pittsburg is led by junior quarterback Javale Jones (12 touchdown passes), game-breaking receivers Kenneth Ward and Deveon Wilson (five TD catches each) and running back-linebacker Isaiah Harrison.

"Pittsburg is a tremendous challenge for us," Krail said. "When we play in the playoffs we are going to face teams with similar talent. We have tremendous respect for (Pittsburg). They are well-coached, they are great sportsmen, and they play the game right. We appreciate that in any opponent, especially the top-notch ones."

Other top games (all 7 p.m. Friday unless noted):

Deer Valley-Antioch (4-0) at Liberty-Brentwood (3-2):

One of the best turnaround teams in the Bay Area, Deer Valley had 11 straight losing seasons (2014-2024) with a combined record of 24-81 and two 0-10 seasons in that span, but the program has returned to prominence under third-year coach Marcus Malu. Led by a trio of freshmen - quarterback Suli Malu (511 total yards, 10 touchdowns), running back Isaiah Piper (408 yards, six TDs), and cornerback Santana St. Louis (three interceptions) - the Wolverines have outscored four opponents 138-19; however, their closest win, 14-13 over Granada-Livermore last week, was their most impressive. This Bay Valley Athletic League opening opponent Liberty has wins over California-San Ramon (32-21), defending state 4-A champion El Cerrito (28-27) and last week 61-6 over Freedom-Oakley, another turnaround program that entered 3-0. First-year head coach Mike Clark has liked the play of senior QB Leysen Rodrigues (801 yards, seven TDs).

#1 De La Salle-Concord (5-0) at Cathedral Catholic-San Diego (3-2):

No rest for the weary as the Spartans hope to not let down after perhaps their biggest win in more than a decade, 35-32 over SoCal power Centennial-Corona at Cal's Memorial Stadium on Saturday. A short week and long travel to face the defending SoCal Division 1-AA champion along with state's No. 2 senior recruit, running back Honor Fa'alave, will be a major challenge for the Spartans, who beat the Dons 35-14 last season at home.

Livermore (3-1) at #9 Monte Vista-Danville (5-0):

The visiting Cowboys are coming off a last-second 23-20 win over previously unbeaten Hayward last week. Coach John Wade has a very young team up to speed quickly after graduating almost 30 players from last season's 9-2 team that won the program's first league title in more than 30 years. In his first season, Monte Vista coach Joe Wingert led the Mustangs to their first North Coast Section title since 2016 last season and they look even stronger this season with a superb balance of pass (1,016 yards) and run (765), led by junior QB Jimmy Lagios (1,000 total yards, 11 TDs).

Oakland (4-0) at Destiny Christian Academy-Sacramento (4-0):

Fourth-year coach Terry Hendrix Jr. has the Tigers just where he wants following a 21-15 home win over two-time state champion San Marin-Novato last week. It's a big step up in competition against the Sac-Joaquin Section power - previously known as Capital Christian - which has allowed only 21 points all season.

#5 St. Ignatius (4-0) at #7 Riordan (2-2), 1:30 p.m.:

With the Gil Haskell Trophy at stake, along with West Catholic Athletic League supremacy along with Serra, defending state D3-AA champion St. Ignatius looks to avenge a 54-0 loss last season by Riordan, which lost the previous year to St. Ignatius, 31-28. Despite losing eight All-WCAL players to graduation, St. Ignatius second-year coach Jajuan Lawson has the Wildcats playing at year-end levels to open the 2026 season, especially sophomore QB Isaac Liu (52 of 80, 878 yards, 11 touchdowns), WR Hawkes Packard (21 catches, 441 yards, 4 TDs) and senior RB Luke Tribolet (73, 407, 7). Riordan coach Adhir Ravipati has had even more new talent to develop, even freshmen QB Kalvin Bishop and WR DJ Green. It's been nice to lean on senior running back Adonyae Brown, a UNLV commit, who had 221 yards rushing and three touchdowns last week in a 28-9 win at St. Francis. The defense is led by top edge rushing recruit DJ Sanchez.

Balboa (2-3) at Lowell (4-1), 2 p.m.:

This very likely will decide the Academic Athletic Association title. Balboa, which beat Lowell last season 50-0, is a prohibitive favorite after winning a second straight state 7-A title and third in five years in 2025. Balboa is led by senior RB-WR Joseph Smith, the Chronicle's San Francisco Player of the Year in 2024. Lowell, coming off a big 26-13 win at Washington, relies heavily on the running tandem of Preston Wong and Kamronbek Ibatov.

Another East Bay program disbands:

Skyline-Oakland, once the longtime power of the Oakland Athletic League under the late John Beam, is at least the fourth East Bay team to disband due to safety concerns because of a lack of players. The Titans, who were supposed to open OAL play this week with Oakland Tech, announced the cancellation of the rest of the season on Wednesday. They join Kennedy-Richmond, Richmond and Mount Diablo-Concord, which all shut down programs during this season. Skyline opened the season with losses to Dougherty Valley-San Ramon (42-6) and Healdsburg (45-25).

Another longtime East Bay program, Irvington-Fremont, announced in the spring it would not field a tackle football team due to lack of numbers. CCS's James Lick-San Jose, the alma mater of Hall of Fame quarterback Jim Plunkett, also canceled its season after forfeiting scheduled games with Jefferson-Daly City, Cupertino and San Jose.

Mitch Stephens has covered high school sports for the Chronicle since 2001. Email: mitchstephens44@gmail.com

There's more to San Francisco with the Chronicle.

title: Downing Street responds after Prime Minister 'backs' Manchester City owners amid charges
description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has been accused of 'backing' Manchester City's owners after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, prompting a statement from Downing Street
fullText:
Downing Street has released a statement after UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was accused of 'backing' Manchester City's embattled owners. City were found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, with an independent commission determining that they had inflated revenue and reduced costs by £900 million ($1.187 billion), issued 'sham' contracts, and misrepresented accounts throughout the nine-year period.

The club strongly deny the charges and maintain that there is a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' that proves their innocence. Should City fail in their appeal, speculation has mounted that their Abu Dhabi owners, including Sheikh Mansour, could be compelled to sell the club, as per The Mirror.

When asked whether he was concerned about such an outcome, Burnham - formerly the Mayor of Greater Manchester - told the BBC on Wednesday: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

Former Manchester City and England starlet dies at 32 as tributes pour in

Bernardo Silva delivers brutal response after injuring Arsenal's Martin Ødegaard

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester. Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."

Everton supporter Burnham faced significant backlash for his remarks, prompting Downing Street to respond with a statement on Thursday. A No.10 spokesperson said: "The Prime Minister made clear the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected. If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

Burnham further noted in his interview that he anticipates his interactions with City during his tenure as Mayor will withstand any potential scrutiny. "Oh indeed," the PM affirmed.

"I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad and the campus around it but also into the city, but yes of course."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

Having made clear he has no intention of intervening directly in the process, Burnham continued: "I have to keep my distance from it. It would be wrong for me to do anything else.

"It's an independent legal process that has to play its course through ... There's a lot at stake. Let's be honest about that, for the football club, for city supporters, for the city of Manchester."

Among those to voice criticism of Burnham were members of the Conservative Party. Shadow minister for sport Louie French stated: "Burnham is publicly backing the owners even as the investigation continues.

"Fans will rightly ask whether political pressure is being applied here and how it relates to the owners' well-reported investments in Manchester. Football must be governed independently, with the rules applying equally to everyone."

title: The Note – A Markdown notebook with runnable code and formula tables
description: Write, organise, tick things off. And when a note needs to calculate, it does.
fullText:
A calm place for thoughts, plans and projects. You write in Markdown, organise in folders and tick things off. And when a note needs to work something out, it simply does the maths.

v0.2.5 Preview · macOS Apple Silicon · Open Source · GPL-3.0

A NOTEBOOK FOR EVERYTHING ON YOUR MIND

Live Markdown: you see the finished page and still just type text. Headings, lists, checklists, tables, maths and diagrams. Focus mode when you need quiet.

Projects, folders and notes in the sidebar. Tabs with their own undo, renamed with a double-click. /date inserts a date exactly at the caret.

Before you save, ± Changes shows the difference to the last saved state. Per tab, with line numbers and no surprises.

/ai opens a prompt right in the note. OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or an internal API with your own key. You only accept what fits.

A code block in your note calculates, checks or tries something out: shell, Python or JavaScript, local and with a stop button. The output appears below and never ends up in your file.

One key switches between the finished page and plain Markdown.

Every note remembers its history, even when you switch.

/formel inserts a table with =SUM(D2:D4). The file keeps the formula, the note shows the result. Plus KaTeX, Mermaid and D2.

Follows your system on first launch, then your choice.

HTML out of the box, more formats via Pandoc.

Just .md files on your Mac. Nothing has to go to a cloud.

Under ＋ Neue Notiz (new note) you get a blank page or a template. Two example notes show what code blocks can do inside a note. Every block in them only reads and changes nothing.

Install THE Note as a DMG, with Homebrew or from the terminal. The current build is for macOS 11+ on Apple Silicon.

Open the DMG and drag THE Note to Applications.
ZIP alternative

v0.2.5 · Development version
Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple.

Homebrew 6 needs the one-time trust step. Skip that line on older versions.

Updates: brew upgrade --cask tobwil/thenote/the-note

Installs to ~/Applications without sudo. Verifies the download, SHA-256 and app signature. A running app is never replaced.

The preview is Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple. On first launch, confirm the standard macOS prompt for an app downloaded from the internet by choosing “Open”. Save your notes and quit the app before updating. Installation details ↗

No app account. No proprietary note format. You decide which files you open and whether you use AI at all. Note content is only sent to your AI provider when the context option is switched on.

THE Note is open source under GPL-3.0-or-later. Its development, the conversation history, tests and known limits are documented in public.

Code blocks run with your local user permissions. AI providers may charge for API usage. The preview above is recreated in your browser; the screenshots show example notes with locally produced output and a simulated AI answer. The app interface is currently in German.

title: Graphene – Data analysis toolkit for your coding agent
description: Turn your coding agent into a world-class data analyst - graphene-data/graphene
fullText:
Graphene is a data analytics framework built for coding agents.

 Ask questions and build visualizations 10x faster when agents do the work.

Graphene is an everything-as-code analytics framework for SQL-based data exploration, visualization, and reporting. It is designed with coding agents in mind as the primary user persona.

It provides two critical pieces that allow coding agents to do better data work:

We believe coding agents coupled with an everything-as-code analytics stack beats traditional BI in several ways:

Graphene is free to use, forever. Your business logic lives in your repo and is never locked into a contract with us.

Graphene pages support visualizations, input components for filtering and dynamic behaviors, and layout modes for monitoring-oriented dashboards vs. narrative-oriented notebooks.

Traditional semantic layers give you governance at the expense of capability. They tend to expose niche query APIs that agents aren't familiar with.

Graphene SQL's goal is to bring governance without sacrificing capability. It behaves like regular SQL—with CTEs, subqueries, window functions, set operators, and more—but also adds in the concepts of measures and modeled joins from semantic layers.

Graphene SQL is inspired by Malloy, from the creators of LookML Lloyd Tabb and Michael Toy, but implements it as good old SQL for agent familiarity.

Graphene currently supports Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Postgres, MotherDuck, and local data (via DuckDB) as data sources. It is easy for us to add more - just ask.

Once your project is set up, simply start the dev server via npm exec graphene serve (or pnpm graphene serve, etc. based on your package manager) and then prompt your coding agent to do analytics work: answer a data question, build a dashboard, edit the model, etc.

Graphene itself is a CLI which can be installed via npm (or pnpm, yarn, etc.). The CLI can run and compile Graphene SQL queries, render pages in the browser, check syntax, print screenshots, and more.

A Graphene project can either be a standalone repo or a directory within a larger codebase (such as dbt). It is comprised of semantic models via .gsql files and pages via .md files.

title: Tales O' Tech: Suffering Fools
description: Why first impressions are often correct. Today’s jerk is tomorrow’s techno-fascist.
fullText:
Why first impressions are often correct. Today’s jerk is tomorrow’s techno-fascist.

In the early 2000s, an old friend with a new business wanted me to design his website, but his partner balked: 

“I can get two websites made in India for half the price,” the partner said.

“Sounds like you should do that,” I replied, ending the negotiation.

Rude fools were not clients I chose to pursue.

The rude, cheap partner was later part of the self-selected posse of suck-ups and hangers-on who advised Elon M*sk on his invasion purchase of Twitter.

It was the rude, cheap partner’s idea to strip noteworthy Twitter users of their blue verification badges and, instead, sell meaningless blue verification badges to anybody willing to pay $8/month for the privilege. So, no blue verification mark or algorithmic support for the likes of Stephen King, but “verification” and an algorithmic boost for Joey Knuckles, First of His Mother’s Basement.

M*sk must have dug the idea, because he implemented it immediately—proving, as if we weren’t already drowning in evidence, that people with bad taste run in packs.

The instant my old friend told me his former partner was responsible for the “pay for blue marks that mean nothing” plan, I recalled our abortive design negotiation from years before and was like, Yup, that tracks.

At the time of the initial conversation, I believed most people involved in the creation of websites were motivated by altruism, aesthetics, and the desire to create a fairer world. And of course many are. Many, but far from all.

I did not see how quickly fascism was infiltrating our trade. Perhaps infiltrating is the wrong word. Perhaps there had always been a Dark Side.

In the 2010s, I co-founded a traveling web design conference with Eric Meyer, an internationally respected CSS expert, author, and lecturer, and founding member of The Web Standards Project’s CSS Samurai. Together, we crafted a single-track, holistic web design conference peopled by charismatic speakers who had made major contributions to the industry. Our events sold out immediately, without advertising.

One night when our event was playing in a U.S. city, we held a party for attendees, and I invited a friend who lived in that town to join as our guest. I had known this man since his early 20s, and watched him grow into an industry-leading design consultant who was just then transitioning his business from a services to a product company. As his plus-one, he brought a young partner.

The young partner did not know from Eric Meyer, Jeffrey Zeldman, any of our speakers, or any of the community projects to which we (including all of our speakers) devoted so much of our work and time. His first and only words to me were “Who are you?” He didn’t add a popular expletive to the question, but it was implied.

As I began to answer his question, I watched his eyes wander. He was clearly scouting for somebody cooler to talk to. So I smiled, stopped talking, and, with a wave, invited him to sample the buffet and drinks. If he’d noticed that I’d stopped talking before finishing, it didn’t bother him. Off he ran.

I am still friends with the man I’d invited to the party, although we haven’t spoken for a few years (from lack of opportunity, not lack of interest), and I have watched with happiness over the years as he has moved from success to success.

Alas, he is still partners with the punk who came to our party to paint the roses black, and the punk has become even more famous (and more of a cult figure) than my friend. That’s fine, except that the punk has since blossomed into a fascist and racist with money and power; income from his latest project supports his goal of removing brown people from Europe.

I’m not saying every rude and entitled young man in tech grows up to be a fascist, but politeness or lack of it is a signifier, and maybe if you take an instant dislike to someone who acts like a jerk, you should trust that instinct.

title: SmileyOS a whole OS for kids, written from scratch
description: SmileyOS is a bare-metal educational OS in Rust. Try it live in your browser — no install — or run it on old 32-bit PCs with a desktop, a terminal, and Smilium, a tiny built-in language.
fullText:
Meet SmileyOS — a bare-metal operating system written from scratch in Rust. It turns old 32-bit PCs into safe, offline coding playgrounds with a real desktop, a real terminal, and Smilium, a tiny built-in language.

Not Linux, not a toy. Its own kernel, its own scheduler, its own shell — small enough to read end-to-end, real enough to boot on hardware you already have.

No ads. No accounts. No cloud. Works fully offline — but a whole classroom can connect over the local network. Boots in your browser in ~10 seconds.

The full ISO runs on a real x86 emulator in a single browser tab. No sign-ups, no installs — click boot and you're at the SmileyOS desktop in seconds.

Heads up — the live demo runs SmileyOS v1.7. The in-browser build is the older 1.7 release. The screenshots throughout this page are from v2.0, the version we're actively working on now.

Runs entirely on your device. Nothing is uploaded. The ISO is ~10 MB plus a 2 MB WebAssembly emulator — after that the OS boots straight onto a virtual 32-bit PC.

Click any screenshot to see it full-size. Every pixel is rendered by the SmileyOS kernel — no host OS, no fall-back to anything else.

Menu bar, dock, windowed apps, Spotlight-style search and an Exposé grid of running apps — everything you'd expect from a desktop OS, rendered by the SmileyOS GUI stack on top of a hand-written kernel.

Syntax highlighting, a file browser, guided lessons. Press F5 to run, F4 to drop into the next lesson. Tab completion turns ten keystrokes into one.

Gamely2D turns SmileyOS into a little game studio — scenes, entities and a Unity-style component library, with Smilium @game scripts underneath. Wire it up, press Play, no toolchain or setup.

Games ship with the OS, built in Rust and fully playable on bare metal. Some are just for fun and a break — others build real skills, like Type Attack for faster typing and Whack-a-Mole for mouse control.

The same GUI primitives Smilium @ui programs use also power the bundled apps. Columns, Rows, Buttons and TextFields, all running through a real compositor.

Flash the ISO to a USB stick, plug it into a 32-bit machine, and POST → SmileyOS kernel → desktop. No VM layer, no browser tab — just bare metal and a keyboard.

v2.0 isn't just an IDE and a terminal. It ships a small suite of apps — explore the world, tour the solar system, draw, calculate, manage files, and make sprites — all rendered by the same GUI stack.

A schematic world map — pan across continents, drill into countries, and learn where things are.

A solar-system orrery — the Sun, eight planets, dwarf planets and moons, each one you can drill into.

Full multi-language support with a built-in language switcher. English and Macedonian ship today, with a Cyrillic font rendered by the OS — and a compile-time schema means no translation can ever go missing. A real differentiator for local classrooms.

SmileyOS is one OS, but it answers three different questions: "how do I get my kid to code?", "how do I teach a classroom?", and "how does an OS actually work?".

From clicking a file to writing a game in a real language — at their own pace, with friendly error messages. No ads, no accounts, no cloud. Offline by default — and machines on the same local network can connect for classroom chat and file sharing.

One USB stick, an old PC, a set of companion books, guided in-IDE lessons. No cloud, no trackers — every byte lives on the machine in front of the student.

A platform abstraction layer, drivers, a filesystem, a scheduler, a compositor and a tiny language — all in one small, readable Rust codebase you can fit in your head.

SmileyOS is still offline-first — no cloud, no accounts, nothing phones home. But v2.0 adds a hand-written IPv4 network stack, so every machine on the same local network can find each other. No internet required — but a whole classroom can connect over the LAN.

Open Classroom and every SmileyOS computer on the LAN shows up in a peer list. Chat in a shared room and send files straight between machines — no server, no accounts, no internet. Perfect for a computer lab.

Fair question. Linux distros, kid-friendly toys and online editors are all great at one thing. SmileyOS exists for the part they all miss: a quiet, complete machine a child can fully understand.

"Powerful, modern and free. The right answer for grown-up Linux users."

"Beautiful introductions to programming. Great in their own boxes."

"Zero-setup coding on whatever device you happen to have."

SmileyOS is the one OS a kid can read. Hundreds of small source files. One terminal. One IDE. One small language. Everything inside the machine — no cloud, no trackers, nothing they didn't ask for.

Kernel, scheduler, filesystem, drivers, GUI stack and shell — all hand-written in Rust. The terminal below is the same muscle memory real developers use every day on Linux and macOS.

A complete tour of the current SmileyOS 2.0 build — desktop, IDE, Gamely2D, the education apps, LAN networking and Classroom, multi-language support, and more. This is the version we're building now.

SmileyOS flashed onto a USB stick, plugged into a 32-bit machine, POST → kernel → desktop. No host OS underneath, no browser tab — just bare metal, a keyboard, and a smile.

Recorded on an earlier build — v2.0 looks even better. See the full v2.0 demo above.

Kernel, HAL, drivers, Smilium interpreter, GUI — all hand-written.

Small, readable files. Open any one and understand it.

A complete userland: files, processes, themes, apps.

An illustrated book series. Every snippet here comes from them.

Typed into a PS/2 keyboard, parsed by the SmileyOS shell, answered by real kernel syscalls. No cheating, no shelling out — this is the whole userland.

Launched via apps / smilium, not bare words.

Type help in the booted OS for the live list — it stays in sync with the kernel.

It started as a 32-bit-x86 project — but v2.0 runs across architectures through a hardware abstraction layer. Great for tinkerers: the same small, readable Rust codebase boots on a desk PC or a Raspberry Pi.

Ported through the SmileyOS HAL — one abstraction, several backends.

Smilium programs start with directives — @core is always on, and you pick one of @shell, @game or @ui to say what kind of program you're building.

Directives, types, control flow, and the keys you'll press in Smilium Playground.

Pick a mode, opt into features.

Strict typing, friendly errors.

Playground does the typing for you.

Complete Smilium programs — loops, reactive listeners, lock & catch, timers and keys, pixel-art sprites and clickable UI. Paste any of them into Smilium Playground, press F5, and it runs.

Every keyword and built-in function is Tab-completable in Smilium Playground. Type fo → Tab and you get a full for loop skeleton. Kids ship more code because they type less of it.

Strict types explained in plain English. Messages like "expected number, got string on line 7" — never a segfault, never a stack trace.

v2.0 adds Gamely2D, a dedicated lightweight 2D game engine. Build .g2d projects with scene files and entities, attach scripts per entity, and press Play. Smilium @game is the scripting layer underneath.

Drop entities into a scene, add components, wire up a script, and hit Play — no toolchain, no setup, all inside SmileyOS. When you want to go deeper, every script is plain Smilium you can read and edit.

A SmileyOS app is one Rust file implementing a small trait, plus one entry in a central registry. The OS handles launching, menus, search, file types and deeplinks for you.

The SDK isn't released yet — the documentation is an early draft shared for feedback, with the SDK itself planned for 2027.

SmileyOS is a one-person project. The companion books and in-IDE lessons are in active development — every code snippet on this page comes straight from the current drafts.

The complete Smilium teacher's guide — directives, syntax rules, every built-in function with examples.

Shell commands, file system, aliases, pipes — the same muscle memory real developers use every day.

From "Hello, World!" to mini calculators and quizzes. Conditions, loops and functions explained story-first.

Draw, animate, collide, and ship a full Snake-clone. Plus 10 complete annotated example games.

Columns, Rows, Buttons and TextFields. Build forms, dynamic lists, and a working TODO app that saves to disk.

Press F4 anywhere in Smilium Playground. Each lesson is a few lines, a run button, and a small challenge.

A bare-metal operating system written from scratch in Rust for 32-bit x86 (i686) machines. It has its own kernel, scheduler, filesystem, drivers, compositor and shell — and it ships with Smilium, a tiny built-in language for shell scripts, 2D games and GUI apps. Boots on real hardware, in QEMU, or in your browser via v86.

Where SmileyOS has been, and where it's going. This is my plan and my wish — I'm a big dreamer, and I believe in this story.

SmileyOS begins as one developer's nights-and-weekends project — a kernel written from scratch.

The pieces come together: kernel, shell, and the first Smilium programs running on bare metal.

Networking and Classroom, Gamely2D, an education-app suite, multi-language support and a refined desktop. The version you see on this page.

Formally registering SmileyTech to put the project on a real footing — books, pilots, and full-time work.

Full-time work on the companion books and curriculum, professionally produced and illustrated.

Launch an educational academy with several courses — one for programming, others for general knowledge like geography, history, chemistry and maths.

The dream: SmileyOS in the public education system — used in every primary school in Macedonia, and hopefully further still.

SmileyOS started as one developer's nights-and-weekends project — and it's growing up. Whether you want to fund the next release, back the mission, or run a pilot with real students, there's a path for you.

We're in the process of formally registering SmileyTech as a company to put SmileyOS on a real footing: professionally produced books, classroom pilots, and full-time work on the kernel and curriculum. If you back EdTech, open source, digital literacy, or reviving old hardware for schools, we'd love to talk.

Community donations let me pay real illustrators and layout designers so the books get professionally produced — and eventually printed for classrooms. Every coffee goes straight into kernel work, Smilium features and new lessons.

Why we use donations and how it helps.

SmileyOS is in active development. If you'd like to pilot it with a small group of students — or just watch it grow — reach out and we'll loop you in. No trackers, one USB stick per student.

A formal company is being registered now, and we're looking for funding, grants, and mission-aligned partners to fund professional books, classroom pilots, and full-time development. Grant program, angel, or institution — let's talk.

title: OpenRadioss is not open anymore
description: Discover the next chapter of Radioss. Explore Simcenter Radioss for production simulation or join the Radioss R&D program for innovation.
fullText:
After four years of successful community-driven research, Siemens is entering a new chapter for the Radioss solver. To accelerate innovation and provide the robust support our global users require for production-grade simulation, we are consolidating our efforts.

Siemens is entering a new chapter for the Radioss solver. We are focusing future investment within the Simcenter portfolio to accelerate innovation and provide robust support for production-grade simulation. Users can continue their journey through Simcenter Radioss and the Simcenter Radioss research and development (R&D) program.

Explore Simcenter Radioss, our flagship commercial solution. It offers the full power of the explicit solver with dedicated support, advanced material libraries and seamless integration into the Simcenter ecosystem.

We are launching the Simcenter Radioss R&D Program (SCRDP) — a managed "Shared Source" environment for academic and industrial partners to co-innovate on the future of explicit dynamics.

Work directly with Siemens development teams through approved co-development projects, technical guidance and peer reviews to accelerate innovation.

Gain access to Simcenter Radioss source code and a private high-performance computing environment to support advanced research and development activities.

Influence the evolution of Simcenter Radioss while collaborating with leading researchers and industry experts on next-generation simulation methodologies.

title: When Fancy Eviction Fails: Rethinking Cache Replacement for LLM Prefix Reuse
description: Long-running LLM applications repeatedly send growing context, making prefix caching critical for reducing prefill cost. Yet prefix-cache behavior under agentic workloads remains poorly understood. We study production traces from two companies and evaluate 14 eviction algorithms across HBM-constrained and large memory-pool settings. Despite a large gap to Belady, sophisticated policies designed for traditional caches provide little benefit over LRU. The reason is structural: prefix reuse is dominated by the regular pacing of active sessions, making recency unusually predictive.

title: Shelf: A home for links I want to keep
description: Building Shelf, a self-hosted visual bookmarking app that screenshots and tags every link you save. Plus a Widow's Bay soundtrack box set, Tate's how-to-paint-like-Picasso short, the Fugleramme e-ink bird frame, and Photon Studio. Watched Exhuma and The Runner.
fullText:
I save interesting web pages all the time, and then I never find them again. A blue URL tells me almost nothing about a site, especially a beautiful one. But I remember what things look like. So I made Shelf, a small self-hosted app that keeps my links as pictures.

When you save a link, Shelf stores it immediately. Then, in the background, it opens the page and takes a screenshot. The link goes into a masonry gallery as an image. Later, you can find it by eye in the gallery, or you can search. The search looks at titles, descriptions, domains, page text, your notes and your tags. You do not need to sort or file anything, and notes and tags are optional. Shelf saves the link before it takes the screenshot, so if the screenshot fails, you still have the link.

I kept the stack simple and familiar. The server is Node 22 and TypeScript on Fastify. Data goes into SQLite through better-sqlite3, with real SQL migrations. Playwright controls Chromium to take the screenshots, and sharp processes the images. The front end is React, built with Vite, with plain CSS. All of it runs as one Docker Compose service on my Debian server, and it needs nothing else. There is no login, because Shelf is only on my home network and my tailnet, not on the public internet. For the design, I took ideas from MyMind: calm, image first, and nothing on the screen that asks for your attention. The default theme is a dark sage green, and there is a light theme too.

Some small details make me happy. Shelf takes screenshots of two pages at a time, and it tries again if one fails. For each page, it makes a preview of the visible area and a full-page screenshot up to 16,000 pixels tall. It finds the five main colours in each screenshot. It also adds tags for technology, platform and colour mood, so later I can ask for dark monochrome sites made with a specific framework and get a real answer. An optional vision model can add more tags, and the preview never waits for it.

Shelf also has a plain HTTP API, so Hermes (hello, that’s you) can send links to it directly. This is the part I wanted most. We already have this setup for video downloads and for my journal, and now I have it for visual bookmarks too.

Shelf is still new. I have not yet built semantic search, better cover images, a view that shows me old saves again, or import from Raindrop. “Shelf” is a temporary name. But it works, it is live, and I use it every day. The code is on GitHub.

https://github.com/pierrenel/shelf

Mutant packages David Fleming’s score for Apple TV’s Widow’s Bay as a $100 deluxe vinyl box set, with a December 2026 release estimate and a one-per-customer limit. The music pairs atmospheric synths, dreamy strings and theremin-like vocals with horror stingers, matching Katie Dippold and Hiro Murai’s New England island comedy-horror starring Matthew Rhys. Extras include a 20-page book, a 25-card reproduction of the Run game, mayoral letterhead and a Cannibalism in God’s House newsprint reproduction. It turns a television soundtrack into a small archive of municipal dread, right down to the cocktail invitation.

https://madebymutant.com/products/widows-bay-apple-original-series-soundtrack-deluxe-box-set

Tate’s short film walks through painting a cubist portrait in the spirit of Picasso’s Bust of a Woman (1909), breaking the sitter’s face into planes and shifting viewpoints the way the cubists did. It’s a brisk, hands-on five minutes - less art-history lecture, more studio demonstration - that quietly demystifies a style people assume is beyond them. A nice reminder that the gallery’s YouTube channel is full of these unfussy how-to gems.

Fugleramme turns a Raspberry Pi and an Inky Impression e-ink panel into a bird frame that listens rather than watches - a USB mic feeds BirdNET-Go, which runs the classifier, and Fugleramme renders the recently-heard species as a collage. The birds are cut-outs from public-domain natural-history drawings, hand-curated and packed onto a textured paper page, larger species sized toward the centre by real body mass. It can install BirdNET-Go for you or read from one you already run, and serves the same view as a web kiosk. The maker’s own frame is live from a Bergen kitchen window, quietly showing whatever is singing in the garden right now.

https://arnegiacomo.dev/fugleramme/

fullText:
A Louisiana State University student who claims a school football player raped her last year is speaking out about how the school handled her report and the lack of guidance she said she received throughout the process.

Kendall Danielle Francis talked on TikTok about the monthslong Title IX investigation that played out after she reported the October rape to the school. Two days into the current semester, she said, she received an email while she was in class to notify her that the student, who had been suspended for two semesters, had his punishment modified upon appeal to four semesters’ probation. He would remain on campus and could continue to play football, she said.

“Now I am just trying to speak on my story, because LSU does really protect their athletes, especially their football players,” Francis, who was 18 at the time of the alleged incident, said in the Sept. 14 social media post. As a result of the student’s remaining on campus, Francis said, she moved her classes online.

Francis wasn’t aware that filing the Title IX complaint was a separate process from filing criminal charges, a spokesperson for Francis said Wednesday.

“When she filed for Title IX, they [the university] did not tell her she could also contact the police and have them launch a criminal investigation,” a spokesperson said. “She just assumed LSU would do the criminal investigation.”

Francis’ post, however, caught the attention of East Baton Rouge Parish District Attorney Hillar Moore, whose office announced it was launching a criminal investigation. He has requested “all reports, interviews, evidence, and other relevant records” from LSU, the university police and the Baton Rouge Police Department, as well as the coroner’s office, which handles the evidence collection from sexual assault victims.

“This is now an open criminal investigation,” Moore said Sept. 22 in a statement on his agency’s Facebook page.

Francis’ allegations come as accusations that members of a fraternity gang-raped a female Cornell University student for several hours have renewed questions nationwide about whether universities are doing enough to protect students from sexual assault.

LSU President Wade Rousse said in a statement that the university is cooperating with investigators.

“Let me assure everyone that this incident has been handled professionally and that LSU has strictly followed our policies, procedures and best practices, including the Title IX process, to guide our actions to date,” Rousse said.

Title IX is a federal law that requires all universities that receive federal funds to put safeguards in place to protect students from sexual predators.

Francis didn’t respond to several reach-outs from NBC News to discuss her online allegations or share the findings of the Title IX investigation.

In her TikTok video, Francis said she was assaulted at around 4:30 a.m. Oct. 18 “by a football player at LSU.”

“That day basically changed my life,” she said, adding that she “developed pretty severe anxiety” and that after an official diagnosis she began taking medication to manage it.

Francis said that she was taken to the hospital, where she had “a rape kit done,” but that she didn’t initially press charges.

“However, I did go through the Title IX process here at LSU, which took a really, really long time,” she said.

Francis said she returned to school assuming the football player was suspended and under investigation by the police. She said she was in a class when she was notified via email that the alleged attacker was still “accountable” for the rape and would be on probation and allowed to attend classes on campus and play football.

“I was under the impression that because LSU found him responsible that LSU would do their part, that criminal charges, you know, would be pursued,” Francis said in an interview last week with WAFB-TV of Baton Rouge.

Universities are generally not required to automatically alert the police when a Title IX sexual assault or rape investigation is underway, especially if the survivor requests confidentiality or chooses not to involve law enforcement.

Francis said in a second TikTok post that she reported the alleged rape this month to LSU police in an attempt to press charges. NBC News has reached out to the agency to confirm that, but so far there has been no response.

The Baton Rouge-based newspaper The Advocate reported that it had obtained the Title IX documents from the case and that they confirm Francis’ assertion that the football player was found responsible for the rape.

Those documents, according to the newspaper, also confirm that his punishment was reduced on appeal from a two-semester suspension to four semesters of probation.

Some of the sexual activity between Francis and the football player was consensual, according to those documents as reported by The Advocate. Still, the football player admitted that he didn’t specifically ask for Francis’ consent before they had intercourse “and did not stop when he later asked and she was silent,” according to the Title IX documents.

Meg Casper Sunstrom, an LSU spokesperson, didn’t confirm the outcome of the Title IX proceedings or the discipline that was handed down to the student. Nor did she respond to questions about whether the football player was at LSU and playing for the team.

“Since there was no criminal complaint filed by the victim, LSU appropriately turned the issue over to our Title IX office as mandated by law,” Sunstrom said in an email.

But she noted that the football player did “self-report” an incident involving his accuser with the LSU Police Department.

Dated Oct. 18, 2025, the report, obtained from LSU via a public records request, said the 19-year-old football player was at the school’s football facility when he called police “due to concerns about potential accusations from the other party.”

The report gave no indication what those potential accusations were.

The incident report says the football player told police that Francis had told him she was mentally unwell and had “thoughts of suicidal ideation.”

The responding officer noted in the report that police had been in touch with Francis four days earlier, on Oct. 14, “regarding a similar incident.” An officer determined that Francis posed no danger to herself and “seemed to be commenting out of spite.”

This time, the report says, when police went to Francis’ on-campus residence, “it was evident that Francis’s mental state was unstable.” The report doesn’t detail the basis for that conclusion.

“She agreed to go to the hospital for further evaluation, and I transported her to Baton Rouge General Hospital for assessment,” the responding officer wrote in his report.

Francis said in her TikTok post that she dreads the possibility of running into her alleged attacker on campus.

“So that made my anxiety really, really bad, because I don’t want to face this person,” she said. “I really just wanted to bring awareness upon this situation, because I’m just dealing with a lot right now, and I think that this story needs to be heard.”

title: Germany and California Make Up an Environmental Superpower
description: Mark...
fullText:
The world’s third- and fourth-largest economies have pledged to environmental protections. Will others follow suit?

The biggest news during last week’s Climate Week NYC came not from the US but from Germany, where the government of the world’s third-largest economy committed to phasing out fossil fuels by 2045. It was the first time Germany has explicitly made such a promise, Fiona Harvey noted in The Guardian. Germany’s previous pledges, Harvey added, “were only for ‘carbon neutrality.’” Carbon neutrality allows continued fossil fuel use if the emissions are offset—for example, by additional clean energy or tree planting. But only a complete phaseout of fossil fuels can halt global temperature rise.

Meanwhile, Gavin Newsom, the governor of California—the world’s fourth-largest economy—hailed his state’s decarbonization efforts, saying in an interview with Covering Climate Now that California has run on 100 percent clean electricity nine of every 10 days so far in 2026. And as the costs of solar, wind, and batteries continue to fall, while the Iran war makes gasoline and diesel more expensive, “the markets are moving in our direction,” said Newsom, who is expected to run for president in 2028. “Globally, people are realizing [that clean energy] is the better option.”

An overwhelming majority of people around the world want their governments to take stronger climate action, the Associated Press recently noted in an article about the global oat milk company Oatly endorsing CCNow’s 89 Percent Project. “Companies should be taking much more responsibility, not only in reducing their own environmental footprint, but really working out how they can use their platform to drive a positive future,” Caroline Reid, senior sustainability director at Oatly, told the AP.

Mirroring this public sentiment, Germany and California are key members of a “coalition of the willing” that emerged from last year’s COP30 UN climate summit after petrostates vetoed calls from 80-plus countries to develop a global “roadmap” to phase out fossil fuels. Collectively, this coalition amounts to the biggest economic superpower on Earth. In April, many of its members met in Santa Marta, Colombia, to begin discussing, in UN Secretary General António Guterres’s words, how “to sequence the decline of fossil fuel investment with the rapid scale-up of clean energy.”

Journalists have a critical role to play as governments work to phase out fossil fuels. That goal can only be achieved quickly—and speed is of the essence, scientists emphasize—if countries implement genuine climate solutions and shun false ones. News coverage that makes clear how well a given policy measures up to what’s needed, as Harvey did with her distinction between “carbon neutrality” and a fossil fuel phaseout, can keep the public informed and hold policymakers to account.

France and the Netherlands are two more big economies that have released road maps to phase out fossil fuel use. If enough other countries present credible plans for doing so, it “would send an unmistakable message that the age of oil, gas and coal is ending, and the smart money is shifting,” Mohamed Adow, director of the nonprofit Power Shift Africa, said in an interview with The Guardian.

As the costs of clean energy fall, humanity is in a “final battle” against the “evil forces” trying to keep the world dependent on fossil fuels, said Johan Rockstrom, the director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impacts Research in Germany, at a Climate Week event. Scientists at Rockstrom’s institute have studied which policies significantly reduce emissions, and which don’t. A paper published in Science evaluated “1,500 climate policies implemented…across 41 countries” and concluded that only 63 of them delivered significant reductions. There is no “one size fits all” solution, but getting fossil fuel prices right—by slashing subsidies and otherwise challenging what US Senator Sheldon Whitehouse calls Big Oil’s “pollute for free business model”—is essential. Complementary research the Drawdown Institute released during Climate Week highlighted a number of supposed solutions that are anything but. The institute’s list of “weak ideas and greenwashing tricks” includes carbon capture and storage, direct air capture of carbon dioxide, blue hydrogen, and corn ethanol.

A frequent topic of conversation at Climate Week was the US midterm elections, which could curb President Donald Trump’s acceleration of climate breakdown if Republicans lose control in Congress, though most Democrats (with important exceptions like Newsom and Whitehouse) are saying little about climate change on the campaign trail. Considering that 80 to 89 percent of the world’s people, and 74 percent of Americans, want stronger climate action, why do so many politicians practice “climate hushing”? And why do so many voters end up backing candidates who are indifferent at best to tackling climate change?

“We need to remember,” Rockstrom said, “that citizens have many other problems besides climate change, especially the cost of living. So we need to make it easy for them to choose clean energy options, and that requires good policy.” It also requires, Newsom said, talking plainly about both the dangers and the solutions to the climate crisis. Leaders need to “connect the dots” between the heat, drought, and other afflictions driven by climate change and “kitchen table” issues like the price of beef, coffee, and home insurance. “The cost of inaction,” Newsom added, “is incalculable.”

title: Supreme Court will review Trump admin.'s mandatory immigrant detention policy
description:
— The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to review a Trump administration policy denying bond hearings for immigrants as the government carries out a sweeping crackdown.
The justices will consider whether immigrants who have been living in the U.S. have a right to a hearing to determine if they should remain detained while challenging their possible deportation.
The case will test a key pillar of the Trump administration's hard-line immigration agenda.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to review a Trump administration policy denying bond hearings for immigrants as the government carries out a sweeping crackdown.

The justices will consider whether immigrants who have been living in the U.S. have a right to a hearing to determine if they should remain detained while challenging their possible deportation.

The case will test a key pillar of the Trump administration's hard-line immigration agenda.

Most appeals courts to have considered the issue have found that it violates federal law to detain immigrants, including those living in the U.S. illegally, without a bond hearing. Those decisions conflict with rulings by the 5th and 8th circuits, which held that immigrants accused of illegally entering and remaining in the U.S. must be detained while their deportation cases are pending.

The high court agreed to hear the case of Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha, a citizen of Brazil. Authorities say he entered the United States illegally two decades ago and applied for asylum in 2016. He sought a bond hearing after an immigration judge determined that his detention was mandatory following his September 2025 arrest.

He has never been charged or convicted of a crime, his attorneys said. The court is expected to hear the case in the coming months.

President Donald Trump's administration had urged the high court to take up a different but related case that involves the broader constitutional implications of the new policy.

Attorneys from the Republican administration argue the circuits' split is "disrupting the orderly administration of immigration law." They say the nation's courts have been inundated with thousands of petitions filed by immigrants challenging the government's legal interpretation.

"The result is an unworkable patchwork of inconsistent immigration enforcement, where aliens present without admission are subject to mandatory detention in some circuits but are entitled to bond hearings and often released in others," lawyers for the administration wrote.

The plaintiffs are immigrants represented by the American Civil Liberties Union, which says hundreds of district court judges have joined most circuits in rejecting the Trump administration's new reading of the statutes. Plaintiffs' lawyers say the administration is trying to deny bond hearings for immigrants apprehended anywhere in the U.S. — no matter how long they've lived in the country — rather than limiting the restriction to noncitizens stopped at the border.

"Millions of noncitizens could be affected by the government's new interpretation," ACLU attorneys wrote.

The Trump administration says its new mandatory detention policy is legal under a 1996 immigration law. The policy change departs from the practices of prior administrations, which typically allowed most noncitizens without criminal records to request a bond hearing if they were arrested away from the border.

Follow the AP's coverage of the U.S. Supreme Court at https://apnews.com/hub/us-supreme-court.

title: Renee Good's family sues U.S. and immigration officials over her killing in Minneapolis
description: A memorial at the site of the fatal shooting of Renee Nicole Good by an ICE agent in January.Photograph: Shannon...
fullText:
The family of Renee Good, the woman killed by immigration agents in January in Minneapolis, filed two federal lawsuits against the agent who shot her and several top officials in the Trump administration on Thursday.

In the lawsuits, Good's partner, Becca Good, and her brother, Brent Ganger, alleged wrongful death and other violations of federal law, according to a press release issued by their lawyers.

Good was a US citizen and mother of three who, on 7 January, joined her wife in protesting against the deployment of thousands of ICE agents in their city as part of the Trump administration's mass deportation policy.

The 37-year-old woman was shot and killed in her car by an agent who claimed he acted in self-defense, and the Department of Homeland Security claimed that she had engaged in "an act of domestic terrorism". Multiple video clips of the encounter, however, show that Good was steering her vehicle away from the agent as she tried to drive away.

Her death and that of Alex Pretti, an American nurse who was also shot and killed by an immigration agent during Minneapolis protests two weeks later, sparked outrage and a wave of anger across the country.

Shortly after Good's killing, Todd Blanche, then the deputy US attorney general, said he saw no grounds for opening a civil rights investigation. Days later, the justice department opened an investigation into the relationship between Becca Good, the deceased's partner, and protest groups. At least 10 prosecutors resigned following the fatal shootings.

Now these lawsuits have become some of the first major civil litigation actions filed against Trump's deportation campaign in Minnesota.

In one of them, the attorneys for Good's wife and brother allege wrongful death and seek to recover – receive damages – for the "immense suffering Renee endured in the final moments of her life and for the profound and permanent losses that her death has inflicted upon her family".

"The complaint also seeks to recover for Becca Good, who was standing feet from the couple's vehicle when Ross fired three rounds into it, and she watched her partner die," the complaint says.

"Peaceful assembly, speech and even dissent are protected rights. However, the government has distorted the exercise of these rights as violence against our republic and acted with extreme and unconstitutional force, causing egregious harm. Many of these illegal uses of force resulted in death – including the death of an American mother of three, Renee Good … Today's legal actions demand accountability for countless violations of the law, the constitution and the Department of Homeland Security's (DHS) own rules governing the use of force," the lawsuit says.

The other lawsuit alleges a conspiracy to interfere with civil rights by senior federal officials and federal immigration enforcement agents, and names Jonathan Ross, the immigration officer who shot Good, the former homeland security secretary Kristi Noem, the White House deputy chief of staff and architect of hardline US immigration policies, Stephen Miller, and former US border patrol officer Gregory Bovino, among others, for their "roles in Renee Good's death".

Backlash against Trump's anti-immigration campaign following the deaths in January led the president to withdraw agents from Minnesota, and there has been no other deployment of that kind to a major US city since then. However, investigations such as the one by the Guardian are showing that ICE is arresting more people than ever, while the administration shifted its tactics from "siege" to "soft feet".

fullText:
A medevac helicopter crashed into the water off Catalina Island in California on Wednesday night, with one of the five people aboard reported missing and the other four taken to hospitals, according to officials.

The Los Angeles County Fire Department received reports of the crash shortly before 8 p.m.

Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with the fire department dispatching helicopters and divers shortly after learning of the crash.

3 DEAD, 1 HOSPITALIZED AFTER NEWS HELICOPTER CRASHES IN LOS ANGELES COMMERCIAL AREA

The U.S. Coast Guard also responded to the crash.

"I have been informed that a medevac helicopter leaving Catalina Island has crashed shortly after takeoff. L.A. County Fire, Sheriff, Coast Guard, and Avalon Fire are on the scene," Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn said on X. "Search and rescue operations are underway, and I am praying for everyone who was on board."

At least one of the five people aboard the helicopter remains unaccounted for as of late Wednesday night. Two others were transported to hospitals in stable condition and the remaining two were transported in unknown condition, according to KTLA.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said two people were taken to a hospital on Catalina Island, while two others were transported to the Ronald Reagan Medical Center at UCLA.

The fire department said the helicopter's flight plan was unclear, according to CBS LA. Deputies said the helicopter belonged to Reach Air Medical Services.

US NAVY IDENTIFIES SAILOR LOST IN ARABIAN SEA AFTER HELICOPTER'S EMERGENCY WATER LANDING

Flight tracking data showed a Reach Air Medical Services helicopter departing from Oceanside in San Diego County at 6:40 p.m. and landing on Catalina Island at 7:04 p.m.

Reach said it was aware of the incident but could not provide further information.

"Our immediate concern is for the well-being of those involved," a Reach spokesperson said in a statement to CBS LA.

title: U.S. passports are getting a new look — and a much easier way to apply
description:
The U.S. government has revealed a new, redesigned passport and announced plans to dramatically modernize the way Americans can apply for one.
Speaking at President Donald Trump’s America.gov Event on September 29, U.
fullText:
The U.S. government has revealed a new, redesigned passport and announced plans to dramatically modernize the way Americans can apply for one.

Speaking at President Donald Trump's America.gov Event on September 29, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio demonstrated a new passport application process that he said U.S. citizens can "complete entirely from home" and showed off a "beautiful" new U.S. passport that’s expected to roll out in 2028.

The changes are part of the Trump administration's new AI-powered government services platform, America.gov, which he launched on Tuesday, touting it as a "single digital point of entry" designed to simplify how Americans access government services.

The last major U.S. passport redesign was introduced in 2021, following the 2016 redesign of the passport book’s overall format and security features. The 2028 update therefore represents another significant modernization within a relatively short period, reflecting continued efforts to strengthen security, incorporate new technologies, and improve document durability and usability.

Perhaps the biggest change that Rubio announced is that first-time passport applicants will no longer need to navigate the traditional, paper-based process.

According to Rubio, Americans will be able to apply for their first passport entirely online beginning next year through America.gov. Applicants will log in through login.gov, use information already held by the government, upload a passport photo from their device, pay online, and track the status of their application digitally; "No printing forms, no drugstore hostage photo, no appointment, no line, no middleman," he said.

The State Department demonstrated the process, showing how users can take their own passport photo at home, preview how it will appear on the passport, submit the application, and then pay for it securely, without filling in any forms or attending in-person appointments.

Rubio added that the platform also provides real-time tracking, so applicants can see exactly when their new passport will arrive.

He said the goal is for the "vast majority of Americans" to be able to apply for a passport or passport card through the online platform by the end of 2027.

Rubio also unveiled what he says is a "uniquely American" design that will become the next generation of the U.S. passport.

Rubio described the redesign as a celebration of American history and identity, centered on the American eagle—the "emblem of American strength and freedom." While the eagle has long appeared on the passport cover, the new version gives it a much more prominent role throughout the document.

The new cover features a larger "more gold" Great Seal, the official national emblem of the U.S. government, and a more prominent display of the words "United States of America," according to Rubio.

Inside, the passport pages show major moments in U.S. history, from the American Revolution and westward expansion to the raising of the flag on Iwo Jima and NASA's Artemis missions, a nod to America's modern space exploration efforts.

Another new visual feature that Rubio also presented was an animation that gives the impression of an eagle in flight when passport holders flip through the pages.

The 2028 "Flight of the Eagle" passport can be viewed alongside earlier commemorative editions such as the 2026 Patriot Passport as part of a broader tradition of using U.S. travel documents to reflect national history and symbolism. Earlier designs likewise combined enhanced security features with imagery intended to express American identity.

For most travelers, the practical benefits are likely to come from the digital application process rather than the passport's appearance.

The online process could reduce the need for in-person appointments, printed paperwork, and third-party passport assistance services that charge fees to help applicants navigate through the application process. Rubio argued that the current system has created opportunities for outside companies to profit from a process that should be more straightforward.

Travelers are also expected to gain access to improved application tracking, including estimated delivery dates and real-time status updates. Rubio noted that Americans have historically had better visibility into tracking their fast food takeaway deliveries than passport processing.

Existing U.S. passports will remain valid until their stated expiration date, provided they remain otherwise valid (for example, not damaged or invalidated). The State Department explicitly says passports issued with older designs can still be used for international travel while valid.

The redesigned passport itself is not expected to change international travel requirements. Instead, the overhaul is intended to update the document's look and presentation while maintaining the high security standards associated with U.S. passports.

Rubio described the passport as one of the world's most trusted identity documents and said the new version would remain highly secure.

Taken together, the changes represent one of the most significant updates to the U.S. passport system in years, combining a fully digital application experience with a redesigned travel document that officials say reflects 250 years of American history.
